Quantum Computing Inc. Unveils Integrated Quantum Security Platform Combining QKD and Quantum Authentication at ECOC 2026

Vertically integrated photonics and quantum hardware manufacturer Quantum Computing Inc. (QCi) (Nasdaq: QUBT) has announced the live demonstration of its unified quantum security platform at the ECOC Exhibition 2026 in Málaga, Spain. The platform provides a single-system architecture that combines high-dimensional Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) for encryption with hardware-based Quantum Identity Authentication (QIA), addressing the classical authentication vulnerabilities that typically affect point-to-point QKD deployments.

The system leverages QCi’s patented Quantum Zero-Knowledge Proof (QZKP) technology, allowing communicating nodes to verify identity and private cryptographic credentials without transmitting underlying data or relying on classical computational trust assumptions. Operating in a compact, room-temperature form factor compatible with existing telecommunications fiber networks, the platform uses time-frequency and polarization-entangled photon sources alongside wavelength-division multiplexing to support multi-node network expansion.

In addition to its optical communications suite, QCi showcased its flexible quantum instrumentation and metrology tools alongside thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) photonic integrated components manufactured at its semiconductor fab facility. The live demonstration was complemented by a technical presentation in the ECOC Product Focus Theatre detailing quantum-authenticated network security frameworks for critical infrastructure.
